title: The Product Friction Review
subtitle: Help CS explain the customer problem clearly, let Product make the call, and give the customer an honest answer.
intro_text: Use this before a Product Friction Review. Complete the five-part brief, run the 30-minute review, then record what the customer team can honestly communicate. This tool does not promise a delivery date.
scoring_note: Score readiness from 1 to 5 in each section. A low score means the request is not ready for a Product decision.
closing_quote: The goal is not to win every roadmap argument. The goal is to end backlog ambiguity.
next_action: Complete the weakest part of the brief before asking Product for an answer. Then book one review and record the answer, owner, and date.
interpretation: The customer problem is clear enough for Product to answer.
Close the lowest-scoring evidence gap before review.
Important context is missing. Return it to the person who prepared the brief.
This is still a request or escalation, not a clear customer problem.

sections.title: Customer Consequence
sections.why_it_matters: Product cannot assess a complaint that has no defined user, workflow, or consequence.
rows: Action the user is trying to complete
What happens when the action fails
How often and for whom it occurs
rubric: Clear user, workflow, consequence, and frequency
Some context but material ambiguity remains
Request is only a solution statement

sections.title: Evidence and Workaround
sections.why_it_matters: Separate observed behaviour from account-team inference, then show the cost and limits of the current workaround.
rows: Steps, product area, expected and actual behaviour
Screenshots, logs, quotes, or ticket references
Current method, operator, frequency, and limits
rubric: Reproducible evidence and workaround limits are clear
Evidence exists but important unknowns remain
Only urgency or hearsay is provided

sections.title: Commercial Timing and Privacy
sections.why_it_matters: Explain the next customer decision without spreading sensitive account data into broad product channels.
rows: Renewal, rollout, review, expansion, or checkpoint
Do not call all friction renewal risk
When the customer will make that decision
Use a real date, not soon
Why this friction affects that decision
Do not paste contract value publicly
A request is not a commitment
rubric: Decision, date, context, and prior promises are clear
Timing is known but the causal link is weak
Revenue pressure is asserted without context

sections.title: Decision and Follow-through
sections.why_it_matters: Every accepted packet needs an explicit state, owner, answer date, and customer communication plan.
rows: State scope and what is not promised
Specific unknown, owner, and answer date
Share when the next answer arrives
Give a direct answer without backlog theatre
Do not imply Product has accepted it
rubric: State, owner, date, and communication are recorded
Decision exists but follow-through is incomplete
Request returns to the backlog without a decision
